title: AI Methods Across Projects
author: Mark Scicluna
subtitle: AI features, approaches and methods by project: how each is used and what it does

projects.name: AgentOne
projects.what: A self-scaffolding agent platform. The user describes a goal in plain language; an LLM designs the agent (system prompt, tool schemas and Python tool code) at runtime, then the agent runs as that purpose-built agent. Agents lead teams of worker agents and can be published as MCP tools for other apps to call.

rows.how: A bootstrap call returns a JSON AgentConfig: persona, system prompt, tool definitions and Python implementations.
rows.does: Turns a plain-language purpose into a working, purpose-built agent with no code changes between use cases.

rows.how: LLM call → tool calls → results fed back → repeat until the model ends its turn; streamed to the UI as NDJSON events.
rows.does: Lets the agent research, fetch, compute and save files on its own, with live progress shown.

rows.how: Main agent delegates sub-tasks to worker agents (each bootstrapped the same way), run concurrently in a thread pool; split by angle or by topic.
rows.does: Parallel research by a team; the main agent then writes a synthesised report across workers' findings.

rows.how: Past purpose → config pairs are embedded (Gemini / nomic-embed-text) and retrieved by cosine similarity into the bootstrap prompt.
rows.does: New agents are designed from proven examples instead of from scratch each time.

rows.method: MCP client (tool use via Model Context Protocol)
rows.how: A vetted registry of MCP servers (time, fetch, Tavily and Exa web search) offered to the model; calls routed to the real servers.
rows.does: Agents pick real, trusted tools instead of writing their own; search fails over Tavily → Exa on quota limits.

rows.how: A separate Streamable-HTTP MCP process exposes every published agent as one callable tool.
rows.does: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, jobfit or another app can call an AgentOne agent directly.

rows.how: Gemini → Cloudflare Workers AI (hosted Qwen) → Ollama (local); quota errors pause a provider until reset.
rows.does: Keeps the app answering when a provider is down, rate-limited or out of credit.

rows.how: Each (provider, model) pair is an arm, rewarded by self-evaluation pass/fail history.
rows.does: Recommends the best-performing model on the Setup screen while still exploring untried ones.

rows.how: Checks on bootstrap output, chat replies, tool calls and worker delegation, each recorded with the model that produced it.
rows.does: Measures quality per model and feeds the bandit; flags weak replies.

rows.how: A separate, tool-less judge call screens replies against the out-of-scope list; one regenerate, then a code-written decline.
rows.does: Hard-to-bypass topic restriction that isn't swayed by multi-turn persuasion or injected page text.

rows.how: Compile check, AST scan for undefined names, regex for forbidden calls and fake local endpoints; one retry then drop the tool.
rows.does: Catches hallucinated helper calls at build time instead of failing mid-chat.

rows.how: Each tool call runs in a fresh child process: scrubbed environment, timeout, rlimits, network namespace, import allowlist.
rows.does: Makes running model-written code safe enough to expose publicly.

rows.method: Layered spec enforcement (soft vs hard limits)
rows.how: Structured spec routed to prompt (meaning), post-generation fixes and a runtime tool allow-list gate (mechanical).
rows.does: Guarantees what code can guarantee (tools, limits, names) and is honest about what only the prompt can ask.

rows.how: JSON schema in the prompt; on a JSONDecodeError the correction retry gets a hint matched to the error shape.
rows.does: Reliable machine-readable configs from free-text models.

rows.how: Focus topics embedded and compared against each other and saved topics, with per-model thresholds.
rows.does: Flags near-duplicate topics and suggests related ones before an agent is built.

rows.how: Model writes a brief of the job and proposes 3–5 deliverables (report, chart, spreadsheet…); code guarantees the chosen outputs.
rows.does: Moves the product from 'a chat' toward a set of useful outputs the agent judges best for the job.

rows.how: Fixed cases × model arms × repeats, with tool responses recorded once and replayed; fixed judge model; published scoreboard.
rows.does: Repeatable, like-for-like model comparison (pass rate, latency, tokens, cost per task).

rows.how: Timed spans for every LLM call, tool and worker (tokens, model, latency) streamed to the UI and the server log.
rows.does: The 'case file' view shows exactly how each answer and each agent was produced.

rows.how: Agents answer with Mermaid diagrams where they beat prose; image generation via Gemini → Hugging Face cascade.
rows.does: Charts, flows and images instead of walls of text.

projects.name: jobfit (JobFit AI)
projects.tag: ASP.NET Core (.NET 10) + TypeScript SPA · live at jobfit.carkus.com
projects.what: An authenticated job-fit trainer: build a profile, paste or search for a job, get an honest fit appraisal with gaps, a cover letter, a job-targeted CV PDF and a training plan.

rows.how: AgentOne (MCP) → ChattyPrayers gateway → OpenAI → Anthropic → Gemini → Ollama; availability via free health pings cached 5 minutes.
rows.does: Always gets an answer from the best available provider without paying for availability checks.

rows.how: The recommendation discussion runs every available provider concurrently (Task.WhenAll) and combines them.
rows.does: Several independent model opinions on the same appraisal.

rows.how: A concrete JSON example in the prompt; typed parser validates it; one correction-prompt retry; heuristic fallback.
rows.does: Appraisals that are always well-formed, even when a model misbehaves.

rows.how: Fit score and label are computed in code from the parsed gaps, never trusted from the model.
rows.does: Consistent, explainable scores across providers.

rows.method: Prompt library, temperature and model tier per task
rows.how: Named prompt templates; 0.3 for appraisal, 0.5–0.65 for writing; cheaper models for discussion and ranking.
rows.does: Right balance of determinism, creativity and cost for each job.

rows.how: Tailored CV and cover letter may only use facts from the profile; contact details come from the profile, not the AI.
rows.does: Rewrites and prioritises a CV for a role without fabrication.

rows.how: Adzuna listings scored by the model: match score, fit note, skills, scam/junk flag, on-target check; keyword heuristic fallback.
rows.does: A ranked, de-junked job feed matched to the user's profile.

rows.how: A job posting URL is fetched and the model extracts the job description.
rows.does: Paste a link instead of the whole ad.

rows.how: Background service sends a daily PDF digest; an HMAC-signed 'Express interest' link generates and emails a tailored CV and cover letter.
rows.does: AI work happens without opening the app.

rows.how: AsyncLocal capture of input/output tokens and latency per call, shown in the UI.
rows.does: Cost and speed visibility per request.

rows.how: Exposes analyze_job_fit, generate_cover_letter, fetch_job_from_url, search_jobs over MCP; calls AgentOne's agent as an MCP client.
rows.does: Usable from Claude Desktop/Code; first cross-project agent link.

projects.name: ChattyPrayers.Api
projects.tag: ASP.NET Core · live at api.carkus.com · backend for AiChat, Moot, Horus, CV_carkus
projects.what: The shared LLM backend for several sites and apps: streaming chat, dialogue, debate, SVG generation and the public 'ask about Mark' widget, plus an MCP gateway any site can call.

rows.how: ILlmProvider with Anthropic, Gemini and Ollama implementations; Claude → Gemini → Ollama with every failure logged.
rows.does: One reliable LLM service shared by every front end.

rows.how: Provider streams (incl. Ollama NDJSON) forwarded as Server-Sent Events.
rows.does: Replies appear word by word.

rows.how: Haiku for chat; Sonnet for summary, dialogue and debate.
rows.does: Matches model cost to task difficulty.

rows.how: Ollama nomic-embed-text embeddings; per-user in-memory vector index; cosine similarity ranking.
rows.does: Find past conversations by meaning, not keywords.

rows.how: Weather (Open-Meteo) and news (RSS) fetched in parallel and appended to the system prompt; failures silently skipped.
rows.does: Timely, situation-aware replies.

rows.how: SVG output extracted from the raw reply; one correction prompt if no valid <svg> is found.
rows.does: Usable generated graphics.

rows.how: A base safety prompt on every request; the public widget is pinned to a fixed fact block and declines off-topic or override attempts.
rows.does: Safe public exposure, grounded answers about one person.

rows.how: Per-IP rate limits and the cheap model tier on public endpoints.
rows.does: Bounds spend from unauthenticated visitors.

rows.how: generate_completion tool over MCP, backed by the cascade, gated by per-consumer API keys.
rows.does: Any site gets cascaded, fallback-safe LLM text without its own provider code.

projects.name: ComfyUI Claude Assistant
projects.tag: ComfyUI custom node · Python (aiohttp) + JavaScript panel
projects.what: Lets Claude read and edit a live ComfyUI image-generation node graph from a chat panel, and adds a node that calls Claude while a workflow runs.

rows.how: Model gets the current graph plus live node schemas, and edits via apply_graph_actions / lookup_node_types tools.
rows.does: Correct graph edits based on real node definitions, not guessed names.

rows.method: Goal → subgraph planner (human in the loop)
rows.how: plan_subtasks decomposes a goal into dependency-linked steps shown to the user, then each step is built and wired.
rows.does: Builds a working pipeline from one sentence, with review first.

rows.how: Keeps calling the model while it signals tool use, rather than keying on specific tool names.
rows.does: Multi-step builds actually finish.

rows.how: ClaudeAssistantNode runs mid-workflow and returns text, int and float outputs.
rows.does: AI-written prompts or numeric settings feed diffusion nodes.

rows.how: Chat history and notes stored beside each workflow and folded into the system prompt.
rows.does: Context stays with the right workflow.

projects.name: baby-meta-agent
projects.what: A from-scratch, no-framework agent course (13 lessons) ending in goal-driven swarms of sub-agents.

rows.how: A goal is decomposed into a dependency graph of subtasks.
rows.does: Breaks complex goals into ordered, connected steps.

rows.how: A structured-JSON call picks tools per subtask from the registry (@tool decorator).
rows.does: Toolset decided per step, nothing fixed in advance.

rows.how: A fresh Agent per node with allowed_tools; out-of-scope calls raise PermissionError.
rows.does: Least-privilege agents; results flow between dependent nodes.

rows.how: One shared local GGUF model, no cloud APIs.
rows.does: Fully private, offline agent stack.

projects.name: Globetrotter (tourguide / tourguide_flutter)
projects.tag: Expo React Native app + Flutter port
projects.what: A location-based tour guide with an AI 'Plan my day' itinerary feature.

rows.how: Gemini may only choose and order places from a candidate list already fetched from OpenStreetMap.
rows.does: Itineraries that never invent a place.

rows.how: Stops returned as JSON with times relative to start; place ids, overlaps and deadlines checked; one retry.
rows.does: A trustworthy, mappable day plan.

rows.how: Candidates capped to the 40 nearest.
rows.does: Small prompts and meaningful choices.

projects.name: Persona apps: Moot, AiChat, Horus, CV_carkus
projects.tag: Blazor WASM (Moot, AiChat, CV_carkus) · Expo React Native (Horus)
projects.what: Front ends on ChattyPrayers.Api for conversations with AI personalities, debates and dialogues.

rows.how: Library of personality system prompts (e.g. Warm Counsellor, Wise Elder) and modes: chat, reflection, letter.
rows.does: Distinct characters with consistent voices.

rows.how: Several personas take turns on one topic (Moot).
rows.does: AI-vs-AI discussion from different viewpoints.

rows.how: Moot's AiPostProcessor runs a reusable follow-up call (e.g. Summariser), preserving SVG/maths blocks around it.
rows.does: Clean summaries without breaking embedded content.

rows.how: .NET stdio MCP server with appraisal, cover letter and job-fetch tools on the same provider fallback.
rows.does: Job-fit tools callable from any MCP client.

rows.how: LangChain + LlamaIndex, FAISS/ChromaDB vector stores, local HuggingFace embeddings, selectable LLM.
rows.does: Question answering over any PDF.

rows.how: React client for ComfyUI's HTTP/WebSocket API: queue prompts, live progress, render images.
rows.does: Custom front end for local image generation.

rows.how: BSP procedural dungeon generation, A* pathfinding, turn-based enemy AI.
rows.does: Generated levels and enemies that hunt the player.
